knowledge:
- key_parameters: mus=A value or numeric vector between 0 and 1 determining the weight of DNA methylation correlation vs. gene expression correlation in network construction ;; riskCatCol=The column name in clinical data representing risk categories ;; riskFactorCol=The column name in clinical data representing cytogenetic abnormalities or risk factors ;; event=The character string representing the event of interest in survival data (e.g., "Dead") ;; doAlLoci=Logical parameter in electGenes to control whether to use all loci or filter them ;; combiningMu=Parameter in computEigengenes to control how expression and methylation are combined
- alternatives: Pigengene=The predecessor package which only uses gene expression data; iNETgrate should be preferred when matched DNA methylation data is also available to improve network accuracy and patient prognostication
- when_to_use: When matched gene expression (transcriptomics) and DNA methylation (epigenomics) data are available for the same set of patients/samples, along with clinical survival data, and the goal is to identify co-expressed/co-methylated gene modules to predict patient risk categories or survival
- pitfalls: Analyzing real datasets with thousands of genes can take a few hours and require 5-10 GB of memory ;; Missing values in DNA methylation data must be handled (imputed/preprocessed) using preprocess.Dnam (internally called by cleanAllData) ;; Ensure that gene expression and DNA methylation matrices have matching row and column names, and sample IDs match clinical data

workflows.name: inetgrate_pipeline
workflows.intent: Integrate gene expression and DNA methylation data to build a gene network, identify modules, compute eigengenes, and perform survival analysis to classify patient risk.
input: genExpr (matrix of gene expression profile, genes as rows, patients as columns)
rawDnam (matrix of DNA methylation profile, loci as rows, patients as columns)
clinical (dataframe of clinical data with patient IDs, survival time, vital status, and risk categories)
locus2gene (dataframe mapping DNA methylation loci to genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Define clinical settings and clean/preprocess all input datasets using cleanAllData ;; 2. Filter and select genes/loci correlated with survival using electGenes ;; 3. Compute gene-level DNA methylation values (eigenloci) using computEigenloci ;; 4. Construct the integrated gene network and identify modules using makeNetwork ;; 5. Calculate module eigengenes using computEigengenes ;; 6. Perform survival analysis (AFT/Cox regression) to identify predictive modules using analyzeSurvival ;; 7. Extract the best model weights using bestInetgrator ;; 8. Perform pathway enrichment analysis on selected modules using Pigengene::get.enriched.pw
workflows.code:
# One-step pipeline (alternative)
# clinSettings <- c("patientIDCol"="bcr_patient_barcode",
# "eventCol"="vital_status",
# "timeCol"="days_to_last_followup",
# "riskCatCol"="acute_myeloid_leukemia_calgb_cytogenetics_risk_category",
# "riskFactorCol"="cytogenetic_abnormalities",
# "event"="Dead",
# "riskHigh"="Poor",
# "riskLow"="Favorable")
# inetgrator <- iNETgrate(Data=toyRawAml, clinSettings=clinSettings,
#                         saveDir="iNETgrateOut", mus=0.6)

# Step-by-step pipeline
resPath <- file.path(tempdir(), "iNETgrateRes") ## the result path
message(paste("Results will be saved in:", resPath, sep="\n"))
netPath <- file.path(resPath, "net")
survivalPath <- file.path(netPath, "surv")
dir.create(survivalPath, showWarnings=FALSE, recursive=TRUE)

riskCatCol <- "acute_myeloid_leukemia_calgb_cytogenetics_risk_category"
riskFactorCol <- "cytogenetic_abnormalities"
cleanedToy <- cleanAllData(genExpr=toyRawAml$genExpr,
                            genExprSampleInfo=toyRawAml$genExprSampleInfo, 
                            rawDnam=toyRawAml$rawDnam, savePath=resPath, 
                            clinical=toyRawAml$clinical, 
                            riskCatCol=riskCatCol, riskFactorCol=riskFactorCol, 
                            riskHigh="Poor", riskLow="Favorable", 
                            verbose=1)

data(toyCleanedAml)
cleaned <- toyCleanedAml
elected <- electGenes(genExpr=cleaned$genExpr, dnam=cleaned$dnam,
                       survival=cleaned$survival, savePath=resPath, 
                       event="Dead", locus2gene=cleaned$locus2gene, 
                       doAlLoci=FALSE, verbose=1)

patientLabel <- setNames(as.character(cleaned$survival$Risk1),
                         nm=rownames(cleaned$survival))
inBoth <- intersect(colnames(cleaned$dnam), names(patientLabel))
computedEloci <- computEigenloci(dnam=cleaned$dnam[ ,inBoth],
    Labels=patientLabel[inBoth],
    geNames=elected$unionGenes,
    locus2gene=cleaned$locus2gene,
    plotPath=resPath,
    Label1="Low", Label2="High",
    verbose=1)

eigenloci <- computedEloci$eigenloci
madeNet <- makeNetwork(genExpr=cleaned$genExpr, eigenloci=eigenloci,
                            geNames=elected$unionGenes, mus=0.6, 
                            doRemoveTOM=TRUE, outPath=netPath, 
                            verbose=1)
print(madeNet$mu2modules[,1:5, drop=FALSE])               

e1 <- computEigengenes(genExpr=cleaned$genExpr, eigenloci=eigenloci, 
                          netPath=netPath, geNames=elected$unionGenes,
                          Labels=patientLabel, Label1="Low", 
                          Label2="High", mus=c(0.6), combiningMu=NA,
                          doIgnoreNas=TRUE, survival=cleaned$survival, 
                          event="Dead", verbose=1, 
                          mu2modules=madeNet$mu2modules)

s1 <- analyzeSurvival(survival=cleaned$survival, 
                        favRisk="High", 
                        subSet="Int", mus=0.6, 
                        netPath=netPath, outPath=survivalPath, 
                        xmax1=15, xmin1=0, verbose=1)

inetgrator <- bestInetgrator(bestPvalues=s1$bestPvalues, 
                  usefuLoci=computedEloci$usefuLoci,
                  lociPigen=computedEloci$lociPigen,
                  netPath=netPath)

selectedModules <- names(inetgrator$modules)
geneList <- list()
for(m1 in selectedModules)
    geneList[[m1]] <- names(inetgrator$modules[[m1]]$genes)
library(org.Hs.eg.db) ## Needed for human genes. 
got <- Pigengene::get.enriched.pw(geneList, idType="SYMBOL",
                 pathwayDb="KEGG", outPath=survivalPath)
